records.title: epic login environment
records.heading: epic login environment
records.body: critical — verify before every shift · when logging into epic, select the ak provider adult critical care environment after entering your username and password. · do not select neuro hosp main campus — this will prevent akron general patient charts, orders, and clinical worklists from displaying correctly. · always verify you are in the correct environment before beginning clinical work to ensure proper access to patient records, order entry, and documentation.

records.title: unit overview
records.heading: unit overview
records.body: akron general's 10-bed neuroscience icu sits within a comprehensive stroke center and level i trauma center. the unit provides multidisciplinary, evidence-based care for complex neurologic and neurosurgical illness: acute stroke, tbi, intracranial hemorrhage, status epilepticus, spinal cord injury, and other critical neurologic conditions.

records.title: part 2 · scope of practice & admissions
records.heading: part 2 · scope of practice & admissions
records.body: admission ownership, trauma boundaries, and who is primary versus consulting. ← start here quick reference start here contents smartphrases the nsicu team manages admitted neurologic and neurosurgical patients.

records.title: primary admission responsibilities
records.heading: primary admission responsibilities
records.body: the nsicu team serves as the primary admitting service for patients with: acute ischemic stroke intracerebral hemorrhage (ich) subarachnoid hemorrhage (sah) other neurological and neurosurgical critical illnesses key point · patients with non-traumatic intracranial hemorrhage are routinely admitted to the nsicu for the initial 24 hours of intensive monitoring. ongoing disposition is determined by the patient's clinical condition and level of care required.

records.title: isolated traumatic brain injury (tbi)
records.heading: isolated traumatic brain injury (tbi)
records.body: admit isolated moderate-to-severe tbi under trauma surgery. nsicu manages neurocritical care with trauma surgery and neurosurgery. after the tertiary trauma survey and trauma clearance, transfer primary management to nsicu.

records.title: polytrauma patients
records.heading: polytrauma patients
records.body: patients with multiple traumatic injuries remain on trauma surgery/sicu. nsicu consults and gives neurocritical care recommendations; trauma/sicu remains primary.

records.title: tracheostomy & peg placement
records.heading: tracheostomy & peg placement
records.body: for nsicu patients needing tracheostomy and/or peg, trauma/sicu performs the procedure.

records.title: critical care consultation for trauma patients
records.heading: critical care consultation for trauma patients
records.body: the trauma surgery/sicu team should be contacted first for icu consultation. if both teams need more expertise, request micu consultation. discuss the case with trauma/sicu before requesting primary micu consultation. interdisciplinary communication · management decisions involving multiple services should be based on direct attending-to-attending communication. early collaboration between the nsicu, trauma surgery, neurosurgery, and other consulting services is strongly encouraged to ensure coordinated patient care and timely resolution of management issues.

records.title: part 3 · daily workflow & expectations
records.heading: part 3 · daily workflow & expectations
records.body: rounds, airway coverage, and required icu checklist habits during the day. ← start here quick reference start here contents smartphrases

records.title: the daily rhythm
records.heading: the daily rhythm
records.body: time activity details 7:00 am arrival & handoff faculty are expected to arrive by 7:00 am to receive handoff and prepare for morning rounds. 8:45 am (m–f) multidisciplinary discharge planning rounds all nsicu providers attend whenever clinical responsibilities permit. 9:00 am daily nsicu interdisciplinary bedside rounds led by the bedside nurse using a system-based approach. 7 am – 5 pm nsicu attending covers airway & emergencies includes code blue events for nsicu patients. after 5 pm micu covers airway & emergency response micu remains available for emergency consultation and critical care assistance.

records.title: airway & emergency response
records.heading: airway & emergency response
records.body: the nsicu attending manages nsicu-service airways from 7:00 am to 5:00 pm. the nsicu team responds to nsicu medical emergencies and code blue events. nsicu apps do not intubate; the attending physician manages the airway. after 5:00 pm, micu covers nsicu airway management and emergency response.

records.title: 8:45 am — multidisciplinary discharge planning rounds
records.heading: 8:45 am — multidisciplinary discharge planning rounds
records.body: primary objectives: review each patient's overall clinical status and anticipated discharge needs. discuss barriers to discharge and care transitions. review invasive lines/devices, including central lines, arterial lines, and foley catheters; order removal when appropriate. coordinate rehabilitation and post-acute care planning. multidisciplinary rounds include care management, bedside nursing, pt, ot, slp, and other disciplines as needed. use them for early discharge planning and coordinated, patient-centered stroke and neurocritical care.

records.title: 9:00 am — nsicu interdisciplinary bedside rounds
records.heading: 9:00 am — nsicu interdisciplinary bedside rounds
records.body: the bedside nurse presents current status by structured systems assessment. the multidisciplinary team develops and reviews the daily plan of care. invite patients and families to bedside rounds when appropriate. icu checklist — required every patient, every day · a standardized icu checklist must be completed for every patient during rounds. the checklist incorporates sccm best practices, including the abcdef bundle, and is available within epic. routine review ensures consistent implementation of evidence-based practices: pain management, sedation optimization, delirium prevention, early mobility, spontaneous awakening and breathing trials, family engagement, and line/device stewardship. · the checklist is part of the progress note. staff can add it to their attestation with the smartphrase .icuchecklistreport

records.title: part 4 · consultation & stroke alerts
records.heading: part 4 · consultation & stroke alerts
records.body: use when a neurologic consult or stroke alert question comes up. ← start here quick reference start here contents smartphrases

records.title: inpatient neurology support
records.heading: inpatient neurology support
records.body: consult neurology for all nsicu patients with acute ischemic stroke, intracerebral hemorrhage, or other complex neurologic disorders. inpatient neurology consults on cerebrovascular patients and partners with nsicu on diagnosis, medical management, secondary prevention, and disposition. at akron general, neurology consults only; it does not admit.

records.title: neurocritical care consultation
records.heading: neurocritical care consultation
records.body: nsicu provides neurocritical care consultation for non-stroke patients in other icus when appropriate. if the nsicu attending is not a neurologist, general neurology handles non-stroke neurologic consults. icu teams may request further neurology evaluation for complex needs. stroke neurology manages hospital-wide stroke consults, including icu patients. always the nsicu team's responsibility · regardless of attending background, the nsicu team is responsible for: · • cardiac arrest prognostication · • liver failure with cerebral edema · • brain death evaluation

records.title: stroke alert process
records.heading: stroke alert process
records.body: suspected acute stroke · any patient with suspected acute stroke: activate a stroke alert immediately. stroke neurology responds to all stroke alerts and manages: rapid neurological evaluation eligibility assessment for thrombolytic therapy (tnk) endovascular thrombectomy evaluation with the neuroendovascular team ongoing acute stroke management recommendations note · the nsicu team does not respond to hospital stroke alerts unless specifically requested for consultation or patient transfer.

records.title: part 5 · emergency transfers & ecmo
records.heading: part 5 · emergency transfers & ecmo
records.body: cct, auto launch, emergency transfers, and ecmo escalation. ← start here quick reference start here contents smartphrases

records.title: auto launch & the cct process
records.heading: auto launch & the cct process
records.body: transfer line: 216-448-7000 (cleveland clinic critical care transport dispatch) cleveland clinic auto launch expedites emergency transfer from regional hospitals to definitive care for life-threatening conditions, including heart attack and stroke.

records.title: acute stroke / ich transfer workflow
records.heading: acute stroke / ich transfer workflow
records.body: step what happens 1. trigger a referring hospital identifies a patient with acute ischemic stroke, ich, sah, large vessel occlusion (lvo), or another time-sensitive neurological emergency requiring a higher level of care. 2. the call the referring physician contacts the cleveland clinic critical care transport (cct) dispatch center through the dedicated transfer line to initiate an emergency transfer. 3. transport activation following acceptance by the receiving physician, cct immediately dispatches the most appropriate resource (helicopter, fixed-wing, or mobile icu ambulance). transport begins while the receiving team coordinates bed placement. 4. pre-arrival coordination neurocritical care, stroke neurology, neurosurgery, and/or neuroendovascular teams are notified per diagnosis. brain imaging is electronically transferred and reviewed when available. treatment plans (thrombolysis, thrombectomy, neurosurgical intervention, neurocritical care) are developed before arrival. the receiving icu, angio suite, or, or ed is prepared. communication is facilitated by epic secure chat, ccf iphone messaging, and direct phone calls. 5. direct handoff on arrival the patient goes directly to the appropriate destination: neuro icu, microangiography suite (mechanical thrombectomy), or, or ed (if additional stabilization is needed). a structured physician-to-physician and nurse-to-nurse handoff ensures continuity and timely definitive treatment. guiding principle — time is brain · early activation of transport, multidisciplinary communication, and parallel preparation of the receiving team are essential to minimize treatment delays and optimize neurological outcomes.

records.title: diagnoses eligible for emergency transfer (incl. auto launch)
records.heading: diagnoses eligible for emergency transfer (incl. auto launch)
records.body: acute ischemic stroke within the thrombolysis and/or mechanical thrombectomy window intracerebral hemorrhage (ich) subarachnoid hemorrhage (sah) cerebral edema with impending or established brain herniation status epilepticus or refractory seizures moderate-to-severe traumatic brain injury (tbi) acute hydrocephalus spinal cord compression or other neurosurgical emergencies rapid neurologic deterioration requiring emergent neurocritical care for emergent neurocritical care, the receiving neuro icu physician or referring physician may auto-launch cct so transport starts while the receiving team coordinates definitive care. cct coordinates transfer, guides stabilization before and during transport, and may contact the nsicu physician for transfer support and management recommendations.

records.title: 1. trigger: suspected need for ecmo
records.heading: 1. trigger: suspected need for ecmo
records.body: consider ecmo for severe cardiopulmonary failure: cardiac arrest, refractory shock, ards, massive pe, cardiogenic shock, or severe shock despite standard therapy.

records.title: 2. immediate actions
records.heading: 2. immediate actions
records.body: stat consults: micu (330-250-1634) and cardiothoracic surgery per qgenda. use early physician-to-physician communication to determine candidacy and coordinate care. resuscitation: continue aggressive resuscitation as clinically indicated. initial workup: abg, serum lactate, stat bedside echo (micu), pa catheter if indicated, portable ct brain if clinically appropriate.

records.title: ecmo candidacy assessment
records.heading: ecmo candidacy assessment
records.body: micu, ct surgery, and the primary team assess inclusion and exclusion criteria. nsicu assesses neurologic status and anticoagulation contraindications as needed. coordinate with neurosurgery and/or vascular neurology when anticoagulation risk exists. document risk-benefit discussion clearly in high-bleeding-risk patients.

records.title: pulmonary embolism pathway
records.heading: pulmonary embolism pathway
records.body: stat micu consult for systemic thrombolysis, catheter-directed thrombectomy, or ecmo when indicated.

records.title: 3. ecmo team activation
records.heading: 3. ecmo team activation
records.body: notify the on-call micu attending (akron) immediately. call transfer center (216-448-7000) to activate the 2shock team, j31 ecmo fellow, and cct.

records.title: 4. decision point: on-site ecmo deployment
records.heading: 4. decision point: on-site ecmo deployment
records.body: if ecmo starts on-site, cardiothoracic surgery cannulates bedside or in the cath lab based on hemodynamic stability. coordinate with cct/transfer center for perfusion support during transport; choose cannulation location by stability and urgency. if ecmo does not start on-site, stabilize the patient and arrange transfer to higher-level care as appropriate.

records.title: 5. escalation contact
records.heading: 5. escalation contact
records.body: ecmo lead: dr. lokesh venkat — 216-212-6977 key principle · early recognition of ecmo candidacy and rapid multidisciplinary activation are critical to improving outcomes in severe cardiopulmonary failure.

records.title: consent & code status (icu admission)
records.heading: consent & code status (icu admission)
records.body: confirm and document consent and code status for icu-level procedures on arrival. code status at admission · code status must be clearly recorded in the medical record at the time of admission — it is a critical determinant of outcomes and quality metrics. patients documented as dnr on admission, based on prior expressed wishes or advance directives, should be classified as present on admission (poa). accurate, timely documentation is vital for patient safety, alignment with goals of care, and institutional mortality and quality reporting.

records.title: icu consent (smartphrase: .nicuconsent)
records.heading: icu consent (smartphrase: .nicuconsent)
records.body: because apps are not credentialed for independent airway management, obtain icu-level procedure consent on admission when feasible. icu consent covers routine critical care interventions, including: endotracheal intubation and mechanical ventilation central venous catheter placement arterial line placement blood product transfusion pulmonary artery catheter insertion bronchoscopy and related diagnostic/therapeutic procedures lumbar puncture (lp) these procedures are standard icu care and may be performed when clinically indicated.

records.title: procedure-specific consent requirements
records.heading: procedure-specific consent requirements
records.body: obtain separate informed consent for non-routine or procedure-specific interventions. general icu admission consent does not cover these and each requires documentation: paracentesis thoracentesis chest tube insertion any invasive or procedural intervention not listed under routine icu care document dedicated consent for each procedure before performance unless delay would immediately risk life or limb.

records.title: progress notes & h&p
records.heading: progress notes & h&p
records.body: most clinical documentation is completed by the apps and residents. during rare high-workload periods, attendings may need to complete one or two notes. during emergencies or exceptional volume, prioritize timely patient care and essential emergency documentation. update or refine notes later as clinically appropriate.

records.title: note templates
records.heading: note templates
records.body: use for template h&p neuro icu h&p regular s/o problem oriented charting cchs · neuro icu h&p stroke care path s/o problem oriented charting cchs progress notes neuro icu progress note s/o problem oriented charting cchs · neuro icu stroke hemorrhagic progress note care path ip main · used for stroke patients so the stroke care path incorporates into the note. for ischemic stroke, change 'hemorrhagic' to 'ischemic' at the top — there is no separate ischemic template. transfer notes .aktransfernote — full template in appendix a problem-oriented a&p .diagpocpoa · diagnoses can be added, removed, and grouped into a shared plan. for problems present on admission, check poa present.

records.title: part 7 · transitions of care
records.heading: part 7 · transitions of care
records.body: pcu/floor readiness decisions and preparing an icu transfer note. ← start here quick reference start here contents smartphrases nsicu coordinates safe transfer from icu to the next level of care.

records.title: who transfers whom
records.heading: who transfers whom
records.body: patient population disposition pathway nsicu primary patients discharged directly from the nsicu team to the appropriate destination (step-down unit, floor, long-term care, or acute rehabilitation facility). trauma patients (nsicu providing critical care) remain primarily under trauma oversight for disposition decisions. transitions to ltac or acute rehab are coordinated by the nsicu team in collaboration with trauma surgery. non-surgical tbi patients stable for the floor transition to trauma surgery or sound hospital medicine based on clinical needs and service alignment. neurosurgical (primary tbi) patients patients who undergo neurosurgical intervention are generally managed and discharged under the neurosurgery (nsgy) service. complex medical needs may require multidisciplinary discussion (trauma, nsgy, nsicu, medicine) to determine disposition. floor transfers nsicu patients requiring ongoing inpatient floor care are transferred to sound hospital medicine (pager 330-250-1576) or family medicine (for established cfm patients). if transfer barriers arise · effective physician-to-physician and team-to-team communication is essential for safe, timely transfer. if disagreements or barriers cannot be resolved through direct communication between services, escalate to the unit medical director and trauma service leadership.

records.title: level-of-care criteria
records.heading: level-of-care criteria
records.body: each patient remains with the primary icu service. nsicu continuously manages neurocritical care and neurosurgical patients during icu admission. intensive care (icu) intermediate care (pcu) general medical floor new, unstable stroke requiring neuro checks q1h or more frequent and/or life support therapies. acute stroke receiving thrombolytics or neurovascular interventional procedures. established, stable stroke requiring frequent neuro checks q2-3h, or frequent suctioning/turning q2-3h. stable stroke requiring neuro checks, suctioning, or turning q4h or less frequent. unstable severe tbi requiring life support therapies. stable severe tbi requiring frequent positioning and q2h neuro checks; minimal respiratory issues including suction needs. stable post-severe tbi requiring neuro checks, suctioning, or turning q4h or less frequent. unstable sah requiring life support therapies. sah post-aneurysm clipping requiring observation for vasospasm or hydrocephalus. sah post-aneurysm treatment requiring observation and neurovascular checks more frequently than q4h, without major evidence of vasospasm or electrolyte disturbance. no signs of vasospasm or hydrocephalus after 7 days of observation; identified as low risk for vasospasm or hydrocephalus. unstable neurosurgical patients requiring a lumbar drain for csf leak. patients with lumbar drains must stay in the icu. stable neurosurgical post-operative patients requiring frequent neuro monitoring. stable neurological patients at 24 hours; csf monitoring q2h or less frequent. unstable or new cervical spinal cord injury. stable spinal cord injury requiring neuro checks q2-3h. neuro checks, suctioning, and turning q4h or less frequent. acute neurologic disorders requiring nursing interventions q1h or more frequently. chronic but stable neurologic disorders (e.g., neuromuscular disease) requiring nursing interventions q2-3h. post-ictal patients slowly waking, protecting airway, needing ceeg and close neuro monitoring. 24-hour observation with nursing intervention q4h or less frequent.

records.title: step-down/pcu vs icu: admission criteria guide
records.heading: step-down/pcu vs icu: admission criteria guide
records.body: use these examples to decide pcu versus continued icu care. make final disposition with the relevant co-management teams: nsgy, stroke neurology, and neurointerventional lab.

records.title: appropriate for step-down / pcu (when clinically stable)
records.heading: appropriate for step-down / pcu (when clinically stable)
records.parentHeading: step-down/pcu vs icu: admission criteria guide
records.body: acute ischemic stroke needing q2h neuro checks, such as icad or ica stenosis, stable after at least 24 hours of icu monitoring sah: no evd; stable or mildly elevated tcds; unchanged neurologic baseline; needs q2h neuro checks and/or close i/o monitoring during vasospasm surveillance ich: stable neuro exam, no continuous antihypertensive infusion, managed with prn iv antihypertensives and q2h neuro checks. escalate to icu if frequent prns or drip initiation becomes necessary. post-ictal: recurrent seizures resolved, airway protected, still needing ceeg and respiratory observation stable neuromuscular disease, such as mg or aidp, with adequate secretion management but ongoing airway monitoring needs mma embolization with stable post-procedure course elective carotid or venous stent without hemodynamic instability stable post-op or post-interventional neurosurgical patients with nsgy/nil agreement stable tracheostomy patients awaiting placement with minimal suction needs

records.title: icu-level care required
records.heading: icu-level care required
records.parentHeading: step-down/pcu vs icu: admission criteria guide
records.body: patients receiving thrombolysis (tnk), with or without subsequent intervention ich requiring intensive monitoring or hemodynamic management post-lvo intervention carotid stent with hypotension or hemodynamic instability nil patients requiring vasoactive infusions, such as aggrastat or vasopressors post-neurosurgical patients with evd or lumbar drain needing frequent bp management and iv antihypertensives cvst initiated on heparin (icu monitoring recommended for at least 24-48 hours) patients with evd or lumbar drains; currently icu-level, with stable lumbar drain transition to pcu under review in 2-4 months operational expectations · icu teams always remain fully responsible for emergency stabilization and acute deterioration management. if a neurologic patient deteriorates, the nsicu team assumes immediate responsibility for stabilization and escalation of care. daytime (7 am - 5 pm): nsicu manages airway and all medical emergencies for assigned patients. after 5 pm: micu assumes airway support and remains available for emergency consultation.

records.title: transfer of care note
records.heading: transfer of care note
records.body: every nsicu primary-service transfer needs a completed formal transfer-of-care note at disposition. use .aktransfernote for all nsicu transfers to standardize documentation, communication, and continuity. include clinical summary, active problems, hospital course, and pending issues. the full transfer note template is reproduced in appendix a.

records.title: part 8 · end-of-life care, organ donation & dnc
records.heading: part 8 · end-of-life care, organ donation & dnc
records.body: comfort-focused care, lifebanc, dnc, and dcd workflow. ← start here quick reference start here contents smartphrases

records.title: comfort-focused care
records.heading: comfort-focused care
records.parentHeading: part 8 · end-of-life care, organ donation & dnc
records.body: for comfort-focused goals of care, place palliative care and/or hospice consults for decision support and symptom management. involve hospice for all cmo transitions to coordinate care, symptom control, and family support. dr. scanling and her team typically lead palliative care consultation. use the epic med comfort care order set to standardize symptoms and end-of-life care.

records.title: organ donation — lifebanc
records.heading: organ donation — lifebanc
records.parentHeading: part 8 · end-of-life care, organ donation & dnc
records.body: lifebanc, northeast ohio's designated opo, partners with cleveland clinic health system. patients meeting referral criteria are automatically referred to lifebanc. before withdrawing life-sustaining treatment or starting brain death evaluation, confirm lifebanc notification. the bedside rn may contact the opo. cms requirement · only lifebanc/opo personnel may discuss organ and tissue donation with the patient's family. the treating clinical team must not initiate donation discussions before opo involvement.

records.title: death by neurologic criteria (dnc)
records.heading: death by neurologic criteria (dnc)
records.parentHeading: part 8 · end-of-life care, organ donation & dnc
records.body: intensivists performing dnc evaluations must follow cchs dnc policy. providers need approved dnc privileges before independent dnc evaluations. find the cchs dnc policy and procedure, determination of death by neurological criteria in adults, v.5, on the cchs intranet under policies & procedures. mylearning: all intensivists must complete the dnc mylearning module every 2 years to obtain and maintain dnc privileges.

records.title: dnc documentation workflow (epic)
records.heading: dnc documentation workflow (epic)
records.body: step action 1 confirm the patient meets prerequisites 2 open the deceased navigator in epic (via the discharge tab) 3 complete brain death exam #1 4 enter the time of brain death 5 generate and sign the exam #1 progress note 6 complete brain death exam #2 7 generate and sign the exam #2 progress note 8 brain death documentation complete deceased navigator in epic (discharge tab)

records.title: donation after circulatory death (dcd)
records.heading: donation after circulatory death (dcd)
records.parentHeading: part 8 · end-of-life care, organ donation & dnc
records.body: patients undergoing dcd follow the separate dcd policy in mylearning. dcd workflow overview

records.title: part 9 · neurotrauma admission & icu management
records.heading: part 9 · neurotrauma admission & icu management
records.body: tbi, spine trauma, polytrauma, neuromonitoring, and service ownership. ← start here quick reference start here contents smartphrases tbi guide for akron — full details available on the teams channel. scenario admitting service critical care key points isolated mild-moderate tbi trauma service sicu neurosurgery consulted for neurosurgical management. isolated severe tbi trauma service (initial 24 h) neuroicu from admission sicu involvement not required. after 24 h, transfer to neurosurgery or neuroicu primary service; trauma signs off. spine trauma trauma service sicu consult neurosurgery or orthopedic spine surgery as appropriate. acute spinal cord injury trauma service (default) sicu workflow may evolve as advanced spinal cord monitoring is implemented; staff-to-staff discussion needed in such cases. polytrauma + severe tbi trauma service sicu + neuroicu co-manage severe tbi with significant extracranial injuries (thoracic, abdominal, pelvic, long-bone). nicu manages the tbi portion of critical care; neurosurgery consultation required. clear staff communication is essential.

records.title: neuromonitoring
records.heading: neuromonitoring
records.body: admit patients needing invasive neuromonitoring to neuroicu (3200) whenever possible. if no neuroicu bed is available, or for selected high-severity polytrauma, trauma may manage patients in one of two neuromonitoring-capable 4th floor icu beds.

records.title: communication & escalation
records.heading: communication & escalation
records.body: attendings should communicate directly about complex cases, management changes, and concerns needing multidisciplinary coordination. for trauma patients needing advanced critical care, such as ards or other complex icu issues, consult sicu first unless already involved.
